thread:
Sam (Support): Hey team — Emma from Tenant Co. reporting intermittent 500s and very high tail latency for hosted dedicated cluster 'dedicated-northstar'. She sent a couple request IDs: req=rt-8f7c2, req=rt-8f7c3. Can we gather repro and logs?

Emma (Tenant): Confirmed — started around 09:15 UTC. Example curl that fails: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -H \"X-Request-ID: rt-8f7c2\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` returns 502 intermittently and one 500 with no body.

infra-bot: Automated note: a monitoring alert fired at 2025-11-02T09:16:02Z for p95 latency > 1s on model-route /v1/generate (dedicated-northstar).

Jess (Infra): Thanks. Can you paste the exact request-id and approximate time window? Also we need one live repro curl and the pod name that served the request if available.

Emma (Tenant): Time window 09:12–09:20 UTC. We only have the request IDs above, and our logs show the client got a 502 then a 500 for rt-8f7c3. No container stdout in our end.

Alex (SRE): Ok. Sam — please ask for a bundle from the dedicated cluster: pod logs, node dmesg, nvidia-smi/top, and dcgm/dmon snapshots. Minimal commands for tenant to run (or we run if they give us node access):

```
# on control machine with kube access
kubectl -n dedicated-inference logs deploy/inference-service --since=30m > inference-logs.txt
kubectl -n dedicated-inference describe pod <pod-name> > pod-describe.txt
ssh node-123 "sudo dmesg | tail -n 200" > node-dmesg.txt
ssh node-123 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv" & sleep 10; pkill -f nvidia-smi
# DCGM snapshot
sudo dcgmi dmon -e -s 5 -o dcgm.csv
```

Jess (Infra): Also grab kubelet logs and the kube-proxy logs on that node, and `iostat -x 1 5` to check disk stalls.

Sam (Support): Tenant can't SSH nodes. Emma, can you run the kubectl logs and describe and paste them here, and run the curl reproduction with `-v` and `-H \"X-Request-ID: <id>\"`? We'll do node-level traces and DCGM from our side.

Emma (Tenant): Pasting curl output for rt-8f7c2:
```
* TCP connection to api.redwood.example port 443 succeeded
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> X-Request-ID: rt-8f7c2
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-length: 0
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```
Emma (Tenant): kubectl logs gave lots of `context deadline exceeded` and a few `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = runtime error: out of memory` messages in the inference pod. Pod name: inference-7f6c9b4d5-xtz9k.

Alex (SRE): OOMs inside container suggest model allocation spikes. Which model variant were you hitting? Jess — could this be related to our quantization fallback that sometimes expands memory briefly?

Jess (Infra): Possibly. We had a config change 3 days ago that increased max sequence length default for that queue. That can increase peak memory footprint. I'll check model routing logs. In parallel, I'll trigger a debug bundle collection on the node that served pod `inference-7f6c9b4d5-xtz9k`. Sam — can you confirm customer approved log collection?

Sam (Support): Emma confirmed via email at 09:25 UTC. Proceed.

infra-bot: Starting debug bundle job: job-id db-20251102-0910. It will collect: kubectl describe/logs, /var/log/messages, dmesg, nvidia-smi snapshot, dcgm, kubelet logs, and a lightweight perf trace. Estimated time 4–6 minutes.

Jess (Infra): Bundle attached here: gs://redwood-debug-bundles/db-20251102-0910.tar.gz (expires in 7 days). I pulled out quick hits: node node-03 shows repeated GPU ECC errors at 09:13:xx, /var/log/messages has a sequence of PCIe reset notices, and DCGM shows GPU utilization dropping to 0 at those times while memory remained pinned.

Alex (SRE): That aligns with transient GPU resets causing requests to fail mid-stream. Can you paste the exact dmesg lines?

Jess (Infra): dmesg excerpt:
```
[09:13:12] nvidia: GPU 0: GPU reset required due to error 0x504
[09:13:12] pci 0000:65:00.0: device reset
[09:13:12] nvidia: GPU 0: gating new activity until reset completes
[09:13:13] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00: returns -110
```
Sam (Support): Emma — this looks like a hardware/transient node issue. We can migrate your reserved capacity off node-03 and re-run requests. Two options: live migrate workloads (brief extra latency) or schedule maintenance and cordon the node. Which do you prefer?

Emma (Tenant): Live migrate please, ASAP. We can't have more 500s during the midday spike.

Alex (SRE): We'll trigger cordon+drain with graceful window 60s and start migration. Jess — please watch for repeated ECC after migration.

Jess (Infra): Cordon+drain started at 09:40 UTC, pods rescheduled to node-07. Monitoring shows p95 latency dropping back to baseline ~120ms after move. No more ECC on node-07.

Sam (Support): Closing loop with Emma and leaving the bundle link. Also flagging infra for replacement of node-03's GPU.

Emma (Tenant): Confirmed reduced errors, thanks. Please follow up with ETA on hardware swap.

Sam (Support): Will do — opening an internal replacement ticket against node-03 (ticket #IR-33421). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
